input: Research NVIDIA (nvidia.com) for a hedge fund

risks.claim: Key-person/governance risk: the board is conducting an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after reports he was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort; Huang admitted in a letter to employees to an affair with a woman US intelligence officials suspected of working for a Chinese spy agency; no completion date for the probe

Market impact: NVDA fell roughly 4.3% on Monday Nov 9, 2026 after the board probe was announced and a further ~4.6% Nov 10 to near 7-month lows, even as chip stocks rallied; the stock had already undercut its 200-day moving average the prior week

Policy risk: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix cautioned the episode could lead to tighter export controls on AI chips, rattling the Korean HBM chain; Huang's House committees appearance is set for Nov 18

A report said the affair 'aided at least $7.5 billion in AI chip shipments to China' via Megaspeed; Huang said Nvidia's business with Megaspeed was normal and it verified no illegal shipments; China's Foreign Ministry rejected the 'so-called Chinese spy narrative'

China revenue excluded: Q3 FY2027 guidance assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China; China was $17B (~13% of sales) in FY2025 and is now effectively closed by export controls, while Huawei's China AI-chip share may climb toward 50-60%

OpenAI single-offtaker concentration: the $105B-capped RVG exposes NVIDIA to unrated OpenAI/SB Energy; Moody's says exposure 'could be significant' if OpenAI defaults and data-center values decline; S&P's debt adjustment reaches ~$37.7B by 2031
Margin risk: management flagged Q4 FY2027 margins potentially falling to 71%-72% on memory shortages and rising component costs; the 74.0% Q3 gross-margin guide sits below the 75.0% just reported

Moody's risk factors: high revenue concentration among a few US hyperscalers that are developing internal silicon; export controls and the rise of Chinese semiconductor competitors threaten global share; electricity supply bottlenecks could constrain demand

Cycle/valuation risk: analyst consensus models a cyclical peak in FY2031 with a 15.8% revenue decline in FY2032; purchase commitments exceed $145B; Rubin racks require 600kW power, 800V DC and full liquid cooling with no air-cooled SKU

Antitrust risk: France's Competition Authority is 'approaching' a decision on formally accusing NVIDIA of breaching antitrust rules; the DOJ previously subpoenaed NVIDIA in an escalated AI-chip probe; NVIDIA is challenging the EU's review of its Run:ai deal in the General Court
Roadmap/execution risk: Rubin Ultra was reportedly scaled back from a four-die to dual-die design on TSMC CoWoS-L yield issues, and Rubin slipped versus earlier Q4-2025 production estimates

catalysts.claim: NVIDIA will host a conference call on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET) to discuss Q3 FY2027 results for the quarter ended October 25, 2026; CFO commentary posted ~1:20 p.m. PT
Consensus for the Nov 17 Q3 FY2027 print: FactSet EPS $2.47 on revenue $108.80B (per IBD); chartmill aggregates EPS $2.53 on revenue $111.356B
Jensen Huang has been requested to appear for a closed-door session with three House committees (Select Committee on China, Foreign Affairs, Intelligence) on November 18, 2026
Vera Rubin platform entered full production (announced GTC Taipei June 1, 2026) with partner/cloud availability beginning H2 2026; Rubin R100 sampling Q4 2026 and volume production Q1 2027
Rubin CPX (128GB GDDR7) / Vera Rubin NVL144 CPX availability targeted for end of 2026, per NVIDIA Newsroom
LPX Rack with Groq 3 LPUs ships fully liquid-cooled in H2 2026; Vera Rubin platform (Vera CPUs, Rubin GPUs, NVLink 6, ConnectX-9, BlueField-4, Spectrum-6) released H2 2026
Fiscal Q4 FY2027 results expected late February 2027 (Q4 outlook 'often moves the shares more than the quarter itself')

OpenAI-NVIDIA partnership: NVIDIA intends to invest up to $100B progressively as each gigawatt of a planned 10 GW deployment comes online; first gigawatt targeted for H2 2026 on Vera Rubin (LOI stage, 'no assurance' of definitive agreements)

event_driven.claim: Board authorized an additional $150B under the share repurchase program, raising the total remaining program to $235B - the largest share repurchase authorization increase in history; expected to be executed through fiscal year 2028
Board approved an additional $80.0B share repurchase authorization without expiration ($38.5B remained at Q1-end) and raised the quarterly dividend from $0.01 to $0.25 per share

Board of Directors initiated an independent investigation, overseen by a committee of independent directors with outside counsel, into reporting that founder/CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort; board says it has no reason to believe national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised and retains confidence in Huang

Agreements with SB Energy: NVIDIA will provide residual value guaranties (capped at $105B initial commitment) backstopping OpenAI's lease and power payments for ~4.25 GW of IT power at the Portsmouth, Ohio AI campus, with an option to extend support to an additional 3.8 GW; obligations commence from 2028 and peak in 2031

Strategic partnerships with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to establish AI-compute financing platforms intended to mobilize over $500B of third-party capital; NVIDIA may provide credit support for up to 25% of financing raised
Filed 424B5 for a $25B seven-tranche senior unsecured notes offering (due 2028-2056), NVIDIA's first bond sale in five years; ~$85B of orders received, demand >4x the minimum size
NVIDIA agreed to contribute $30B to an OpenAI funding round announced in February 2026; earlier commitments include a $5B stake in Intel (announced Sept 18, 2025) and up to $10B in Anthropic
Nvidia unexpectedly revealed direct investments in four Korean AI and robotics startups (reported Nov 10, 2026)

NVIDIA told the EU General Court that the European Commission's scrutiny of its below-threshold Run:ai takeover (approved Dec 2024, ~$700M) rested on an unlawful attempt to expand merger-control remit via Italy's call-in powers

NVIDIA announced a Christmas Eve license agreement with Groq and hired its leadership, committing to a new LPU architecture annually alongside the GPU cadence; Q2 FY2027 cash flow shows a $2,944M 'Groq, Inc.' financing outflow

output.research_view: Everything now hangs on the Nov 17 Q3 FY2027 print: NVIDIA just guided $108B (+/-2%) with 74.0% margins after a $96.2B quarter that beat consensus, and management's own warning that Q4 margins could compress to 71%-72% on memory-cost inflation makes the guide quality the decisive variable. The fresh key-person/governance shock - a board-led independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, announced Nov 8 and already costing the stock ~4-5% over two days ahead of a Nov 18 congressional appearance - has made headline and export-control risk (the spy-report link to $7.5B of China shipments) as important as fundamentals. The financial profile is still fortress-like (Aa1/AA ratings, ~$72.5B net cash, $235B buyback), but NVIDIA has layered contingent OpenAI/financing-platform guarantees of up to $230B on top of it, so the bull case now requires AI-customer credit to hold, not just NVIDIA's.

credit_signals.claim: Moody's upgraded NVIDIA's senior unsecured rating to Aa1 with a positive outlook, citing robust liquidity and a dominant position in data center AI infrastructure

Moody's affirmed NVIDIA's Aa1 senior unsecured and Prime-1 commercial paper ratings, positive outlook, after the SB Energy RVG announcement; pro forma for the $25B June issuance: $106B cash and marketable securities, adjusted debt/EBITDA 0.2x; Moody's expects revenue to grow 77% in FY2027 and 54% in FY2028 with $424B cumulative FCF over two years

S&P Global Ratings affirmed its 'AA' issuer credit rating on NVIDIA, outlook stable; RVG debt adjustment of $4.2B in 2028 (fiscal 2029) rising to ~$37.7B in 2031 (fiscal 2032); pro forma net cash ~$72.5B as of April 26, 2026; downgrade threshold is adjusted leverage above 1.5x

Note tranches priced June 2026: $3.5B 4.250% due 2028; $3.5B 4.350% due 2029; $4.0B 4.500% due 2031; $3.5B 4.750% due 2033; $4.0B 4.950% due 2036; $3.0B 5.550% due 2046; $3.5B 5.625% due 2056; estimated net proceeds ~$24.9B for general corporate purposes including refinancing outstanding notes

Indenture contains no financial covenants and no restrictions on debt incurrence, dividends or repurchases; longest tranche priced 65 bps above Treasuries after tightening 25 bps from initial price talk

10-Q balance sheet (July 26, 2026): short-term debt $1,000M; long-term debt $32,366M (up from $7,469M at Jan 25, 2026); $24,896M of debt issued in the quarter; cash and equivalents $22,443M plus $34,143M marketable debt securities

Before the June 2026 offering NVIDIA had only $8.5B aggregate senior notes outstanding, a $25.0B commercial paper program with nothing outstanding, no secured debt at NVIDIA or subsidiaries, and no secured or unsecured subsidiary indebtedness

Moody's: the RVG contingent obligations amplify downside financial risk - if OpenAI defaulted on lease obligations and data center values declined substantially, exposure could be significant; NVIDIA could materially increase guarantee exposure by extending to 3.8 GW more and/or providing up to $125B of credit support via the financing platforms

missing_fields: Per-tranche maturity dates of legacy senior notes (A2026-A2060 series listed in the 10-Q) - tranche names read but dates not extracted from the filing
S&P Global Ratings rating history prior to the Aug 18, 2026 AA affirmation (only the affirmation was read, not the initiation/upgrade history)
Form 13D (activist) filings on NVDA - none found; only 13G/13G-A filings (Vanguard realignment, NVIDIA's own stakes in Nebius/CoreWeave) were located
Index-change or lock-up-expiry events in the next 6 months - none found in collected sources
Court hearing dates for NVIDIA's EU General Court challenge of the Run:ai review - case filings read but no hearing date given

alternative_signals.claim: Hiring: headcount 47,771 in June 2026 (+3.7% Y/Y); 7,422 active job postings (+114.7% Y/Y); hiring velocity 3,604 new roles/month vs 1,860 in 2025; no layoffs indicated
No-layoff stance: NVIDIA maintains its 'no headcount reduction ever' principle (last meaningful-scale layoff 2008) and is expanding hiring while Meta (8,000) and Microsoft (4,800) conduct layoffs
NVIDIA and Oracle announced an expansion of NVIDIA Vera Rubin to multi-gigawatt scale and bringing the NVIDIA Vera CPU to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
NVIDIA and Meta announced an expanded collaboration on Muse and the Muse family of models 'amid robust growth'
NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a collaboration on sovereign AI infrastructure with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion; Rebellions plans to connect its next-gen R200 NPUs via NVLink Fusion

Archer Aviation to integrate NVIDIA's IGX Thor AI platform into aircraft systems (CES 2026); separately, an Uber partnership trains driving foundation models on Uber real-world data using DGX Cloud (Oct 2025)

Jensen Huang said demand for NVIDIA products through 2027 has hit $1 trillion; CFO Kress confirmed the figure covers only Blackwell and Rubin products and associated networking, excluding Groq LPUs and standalone CPUs

FY2026 (ended Jan 25, 2026) per annual report: revenue grew 65% to $216B; Data Center $194B (+68%); networking >$31B; sovereign AI more than tripled to >$30B; ~9 GW of Blackwell AI factory capacity deployed; visibility into more than $1T of cumulative Blackwell+Rubin revenue from start of 2025 through 2027
Channel check: Blackwell B300 lead times dropped from 36 weeks to 18 weeks as demand stabilizes ahead of the Rubin transition

AWS partnership to deploy 2 million additional NVIDIA GPUs in 2027 and 2028; company projects ~70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, far above analysts' previous forecast; analyst consensus Strong Buy (48 of 52), average price target $328.75 (~51% upside)

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q2 FY2027 (ended July 26, 2026): revenue $96.221B, up 18% Q/Q and 106% Y/Y, beating company guidance of $91.0B +/-2% and Street consensus of $92.27B; Data Center revenue $89.0B (+117% Y/Y)
Q2 FY2027 EPS: non-GAAP $2.22 beat consensus $2.09-$2.10; GAAP diluted EPS $2.46; GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin 75.0%, in line with guided 74.9%/75.0% (+/-50 bps)

Current guidance (issued Aug 26, 2026 for Q3 FY2027): revenue $108.0B +/-2% assuming no Data Center compute revenue from China; GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin 74.0% +/-50 bps; opex ~$9.2B GAAP / ~$9.0B non-GAAP
Q3 FY2027 revenue guidance of $105.8B-$110.2B was above the $103.5B consensus estimate at the time it was issued

Q1 FY2027 (ended April 26, 2026): record revenue $81.6B (+85% Y/Y) vs $78.4B Street estimate; non-GAAP EPS $1.87 vs $1.76 consensus (GAAP EPS $2.39); Data Center $75.2B (+92% Y/Y); Q2 guide was $91.0B +/-2%
NVIDIA has beaten Street earnings expectations in each of the past four quarters; shares rose 8.7% on the Q2 FY2027 report; FY2027 consensus adjusted EPS $9.30 (+103.5% vs $4.57 in FY2026)
On the Q2 call, management flagged margins potentially falling to 71%-72% in Q4 FY2027 and concerns about memory shortages and rising component costs
Consensus FY2027 forecast: revenue $418.824B (+94.0% Y/Y) and EPS $9.48 (latest estimate recorded Nov 7, 2026 from 66 analysts); FY2028 forecast revenue $712.307B (+70.1%), EPS $16.16

insider_and_ownership.claim: Director Mark Stevens sold 1,366,000 shares at $219.73 ($300.1M) on Sept 18, 2026 (reported Sept 22), after selling 1,848,501 at $222.26 on Aug 31 and 1,022,239 at $230.51 on Sept 3 - roughly $947M of September sales
Mark Stevens also sold 1,000,000 shares at $221.10 on June 2, 2026 and 885,000 shares at $210.17 on June 18, 2026 (~$407M of June sales)
EVP & CFO Colette Kress sold 34,918 shares at $219.05 ($7.65M) on Sept 17, 2026; EVP & General Counsel Timothy Teter sold 30,460 at $222.80 on Sept 21 and 30,000 at $217.88 on Aug 31
Director Tench Coxe made gifts of 500,000 shares on July 1, Aug 5, Sept 2, Oct 7 and Nov 4, 2026, holding 28,081,218 shares (indirect) after the last
CEO Jensen Huang (holding 811,521,160 shares) had 45,728 shares tax-withheld at $212.17 on Sept 16, 2026 and gifted 438,000 shares on Sept 17, 2026
No insider open-market purchases are shown; all open-market transactions listed are sales (as of Nov 10, 2026)

13F institutional ownership (Q2 2026, as of June 30): 5,957 managers held 16,793,310,895 shares worth $3.35T; managers filing both quarters added a net 671.1M shares (+4.2%); 2,845 added vs 2,245 trimmed; 218 opened, 120 sold out

Largest NVDA holders Q2 2026: BlackRock $389B (1.94B shares, Added); Vanguard Capital Management $308B; FMR $205B; State Street $202B; biggest buyer Norges Bank (+$65.2B, new); biggest sellers CalPERS (−$4.5B), Barclays (−$4.5B), Capital World Investors (−$4.2B)

Vanguard filed a 13G/A reporting zero beneficial ownership after an internal realignment effective Jan 12, 2026 - no sale occurred; its pre-realignment position was 2,266,625,855 shares (9.32%) as of Dec 31, 2025
NVIDIA's own 13G filings: a new 9.3% position in Nebius Group (22,256,412 shares, July 13, 2026) and an 11.5% stake in CoreWeave (47.2M shares as of Jan 23, 2026)
